# What vim does to a window's horizontal scroll under 'nowrap', measured
# 2026-09-04 against /opt/homebrew/bin/vim, VIM 9.2 patches 1-321, over a file
# of 40 lines of 300 single-width characters each, through
#
#   vim --clean -i NONE --not-a-term -S probe.vim -s KEYS long.txt
#
# with ":set columns=" fixing the window width, winrestview() fixing 'leftcol'
# and the cursor, and winsaveview().leftcol and col('.') read back through
# writefile().
#
# The columns are
#
#   keys  width  sidescrolloff  sidescroll  leftcol  column  ->  leftcol  column
#
# where both columns are display columns, 0-based, so that they are the
# coordinate internal/window works in rather than the 1-based one col() prints.
# The leftcol and column before the keys are what vim reported, not what
# winrestview() was handed.
#
# The "N|" rows are motions and the "z" rows are the horizontal scrolling
# commands; internal/window/horiz_test.go replays both.
50|        80   5   0     0     0 ->     0    49
100|       80   5   0     0     0 ->    59    99
81|        80   5   0     0     0 ->    40    80
76|        80   5   0     0     0 ->    35    75

# Added 2026-09-05, same method and same corpus.
#
# zl and zL scrolled past the last column of the line. The margin column does
# not exist, so vim leaves the cursor on the last character and moves 'leftcol'
# instead: to the character itself when it had scrolled off the left edge, and
# then wherever curs_columns wants it, which centres at 'sidescroll' 0 and
# slides at 1. The cursor never lands past the last byte of the line.
2zL        80   0   0   220   299 ->   299   299
100zl      80   0   0   200   249 ->   299   299
zl         80   0   0   299   299 ->   299   299
2zL        80   0   1   220   299 ->   299   299
zL         80   5   1   259   299 ->   294   299
100zl      80   5   1   259   264 ->   294   299
2zL        80   5   0   220   299 ->   259   299
zL         80   5   0   290   299 ->   259   299
zL         40   0   0   290   295 ->   299   299
zL         40   5   0   290   295 ->   279   299
